subject: Linear combination of multiple random effects

messages.author: d54aba6af40f8c5e
messages.subject: Linear combination of multiple random effects
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to form a linear combination of multiple random effects of different dimensions. For example, say I have

f = y ~ 1 + ....+ f(idx1) + f(idx2)

Here unique values of idx range from, say, idx1=1,...,3 while idx2=1,...,5. Suppose I want the 3x5=15 linear combination of both of these random effects? (I know I could simply predict outcomes here, but I'm working with a more complex structure where slopes and intercepts consist of combinations of multiple random effects of different sizes.)

Apologies if I'm missing something obvious.

Thanks,

John

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Linear combination of multiple random effects
parts:
see also the old-faq in the vignettes.

Best
H
*************


m1 <- 20
m2 <- 30
n <- m1 * m2
s <- 0.1

make.vec <- function(i, n) {
idx <- rep(0, n)
idx[i] <- 1
return (idx)
}

x1 <- rnorm(m1)
x2 <- rnorm(m2)

all.lc <- c()
all.lc.mean <- c()
y <- c()
for(i in 1:m1) {
for(j in 1:m2) {
y <- c(y, 0 + x1[i] + x2[j] + rnorm(1, sd = s))

lc <- inla.make.lincomb(i1 = make.vec(i, m1),
i2 = make.vec(j, m2))
names(lc) <- paste0("x1:", i, ",x2:", j)
all.lc <- c(all.lc, lc)
all.lc.mean <- c(all.lc.mean, x1[i] + x2[j])
}
}

hyper <- list(prec = list(initial = 0,
fixed = TRUE))

r <- inla(y ~ -1 +
f(i1, hyper = hyper) +
f(i2, hyper = hyper),
data = data.frame(y,
i1 = rep(1:m1, each = m2),
i2 = rep(1:m2, m1)),
control.family = list(
hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2),
fixed = TRUE))),
lincomb = all.lc)

plot(r$summary.lincomb.derived$mean, all.lc.mean)
abline(a=0,b=1)
